title: Generating a space without redundancy
learningObjective: Distinguish spanning from linear independence using relations among vectors.

retrieve.bodyMarkdown: A subspace must contain every linear combination of its vectors. What is the smallest subspace containing a given list?

encounter.bodyMarkdown: Two arrows can point in different directions, or one can be a rescaled copy of the other. When does a second vector contribute a new direction?

explain.bodyMarkdown: The span of $v_1,\ldots,v_k$ is all sums $a_1v_1+\cdots+a_kv_k$ with real coefficients. A list is independent when the only combination equal to zero has every coefficient zero. A nontrivial relation signals redundancy: a vector with nonzero coefficient can be expressed using the others. Spanning says a list reaches the target space; independence says it has no redundancy. These are different claims. The empty list is independent and spans the zero space.

reflect.bodyMarkdown: A vector list may span a space while being redundant, or be independent while failing to span the target. Always name the ambient or target space.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Look for a scalar multiple of the generator.
Both coordinates must use the same scalar.
If the first coordinate is $t$, the second must be $2t$.
The span consists of $(t,2t)$. Taking $t=3$ gives $(3,6)$; the other vectors do not satisfy the coordinate ratio.

problems.solutionMarkdown: The span consists of $(t,2t)$. Taking $t=3$ gives $(3,6)$; the other vectors do not satisfy the coordinate ratio.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Match the first coordinates.
Expand the linear combination coordinatewise.
The first coordinate is $a+3$.
The right side is $(a+3,3)$, so $a+3=5$ and $a=2$.

problems.solutionMarkdown: The right side is $(a+3,3)$, so $a+3=5$ and $a=2$.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Check coverage and redundancy separately.
A vector expressible through the others gives dependence.
The third vector is the sum of the first two.
The first two vectors already span the plane. The third is their sum, so the list has a nontrivial relation and is dependent.

problems.solutionMarkdown: The first two vectors already span the plane. The third is their sum, so the list has a nontrivial relation and is dependent.

problems.promptMarkdown: If $a(1,1)+b(1,-1)=(0,0)$, adding the coordinate equations gives $2a=0$. Enter $a$ and then $b$.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Find all coefficients producing zero.
Equate both coordinates to zero.
Adding the equations eliminates $b$.
The equations are $a+b=0$ and $a-b=0$. Their sum gives $a=0$, and substitution gives $b=0$, proving independence.

problems.solutionMarkdown: The equations are $a+b=0$ and $a-b=0$. Their sum gives $a=0$, and substitution gives $b=0$, proving independence.

problems.promptMarkdown: Prove that any list containing the zero vector is dependent.

steps.textMarkdown: Suppose a list contains a zero vector in position $j$.
Assign coefficient $1$ to position $j$ and $0$ to every other position.
This linear combination equals zero but its coefficients are not all zero.
Therefore the list is linearly dependent.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Construct a nontrivial combination equal to zero.
Use the zero vector already in the list.
Its coefficient can be nonzero without changing the sum.
Give an explicit nontrivial relation: multiplying the zero vector by one and all other vectors by zero suffices.

problems.solutionMarkdown: Give an explicit nontrivial relation: multiplying the zero vector by one and all other vectors by zero suffices.

master.notes: Interpret correct first attempts as evidence on these concepts; hints and solution reveals remain visible in the summary.
